title: AO/28/2012 of NEW INDIA ASSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Vs NARENDRA MOHAN NAYAL and OTHERS

paras.text:
IN THE HIGH COURT OF UTTARAKHAND AT
NAINITAL
Appeal From Order No. 28 of 2012
The New India Assurance Company Limited, having its
Head Office at 87, Mahatma Gandhi Road, Fort Mumbai
through Senior Divisional Manager, The New India
Assurance Company Limited, Divisional Office, Opposite
Judge's Court, Nainital Road, Haldwani (Nainital)
Uttarakhand.
.........Appellant

1. Shri Narendra Mohan Nayal S/o Paan Singh R/o
Village Bhanwari, Post Ranman, Thana
Someshwar, Tehsil Someshwar, District Almora,
2. Smt. Maya Nayal W/o Shri Narendra Mohan Nayal
R/o Village Bhanwari, Post Ranman, Thana
Someshwar, Tehsil Someshwar, District Almora
.......Claimants/respondents
3. Shri Manoj Kumar Pathak S/o Shri K.N. Pathak
House No. 11 Badi Bagicha, Almora
......Owner/respondent
4. Visjal Nayal S/o Shri U.S. Nayal R/o Adarsh
Colony, Maal Durgakhaal, Almora.
....Driver/respondents
Mr. V.K. Kohli, Senior Advocate, assisted by Mr. I.P. Kohli, Advocate, present
for the appellant.
Mr. S.K. Mandal, Advocate, present for the claimants/respondents No. 1 and 2.
Mr. Amish Tiwari, Advocate, present for the respondents No.3 and 4.
Hon'ble Prafulla C. Pant, J.
 This appeal, preferred under Section 173 of
Motor Vehicle Act, 1988, is directed against the award
dated 09.12.2011, passed by Motor Accident Claims

2
Tribunal/Additional District Judge, Almora, in Motor
Accident Claims Case No. 03 of 2011, whereby said
Tribunal has awarded ` 4,00,000/- as compensation to the
claimants/respondents No.1 and 2 with the direction that the
same shall be paid by New India Assurance Company
(appellant) with 6% interest per annum thereon.
 2) Heard learned counsel for the parties, and
perused the record of the Tribunal.
 3) Brief facts of the case are that on 08.10.2009, at
about 10.00 p.m. Himanshu Nayal (deceased) was going on
motorcycle with Uttam Singh Nayal owner of motorcycle
bearing Registration No. UA01-2688, from Dugaalkhola to
Sai Baba Colony, Almora. It is pleaded in the claim petition
that Uttam Singh Nayal got down from the bike to ease out
himself by the side of the road and the motorcycle was
parked on the side of the road. It is alleged that the
motorcycle bearing Registration No. UK01-7828, which
was being rashly and negligently driven by Vishal Nayal
dashed at Himanshu Nayal, who was standing on the side of
the road. He (Himanshu Nayal) suffered injuries and taken
to Hospital, where he succumbed to injuries. The deceased
was 18 years old B.A. Part-I student. The claimants are
parents of the deceased. The motorcycle owned by
respondent No.3 Manoj Kumar Pathak, which was being
driven by Vishal Nayal was insured with The New India
Assurance Company Ltd.(appellant). With the above

3
pleadings the claim petition was filed by the parents of the
deceased before the Motor Accident Claims Tribunal.
4) The petition was contested before the Tribunal
by the owner of the motorcycle No. UK01-7828 and
respondent No.4 Vishal Nayal, who was driving the same.
However, it was pleaded by them that the vehicle was
insured with The New India Assurance Company Ltd. and
the liability to pay compensation if any with regard to the
accident lies with said company. The New India Assurance
Company Ltd. (present appellant) pleaded that it is a case of
contributory negligence and the claim petition is bad for
non-joinder of insurance company with whom, motorcycle
bearing Registration No. UA01-2688 was insured. It is also
pleaded that at the time of the accident respondent No.4
Vishal Nayal was not having a valid driving license.
5) On the basis of the pleading, the Tribunal
framed following issues:-
1) Whether on 08.10.2009, at about 10.00 p.m.
Himanshu Nayal was standing on the side of the
road after parking his motorcycle bearing
Registration No. UA01-2688, and whether
another motorcycle bearing Registration No.
UK01-7828, was being rashly and negligently
driven (by Vishal Nayal) dashed at Himanshu
Nayal who suffered injuries and died on
09.10.2009, due to the accident?

4
2) Whether the accident occurred due to the
collision between the motorcycle No. UA01-
2688 and UK 01-7828?
3) Whether the claim petition is bad for non-joinder
of driver and insurance company with whom the
motorcycle No. UK01-7828 is ensured?
4) Whether the owner of the motorcycle No.
UK01-7828 is in collusion with the claimants?
5) Whether at the time of the accident, the driver of
the vehicle was in possession of valid
registration and other papers?
6) To what amount of compensation if any, the
claimants are entitled and from whom?
6) After recording the evidence and hearing the
parties, the Tribunal found that due to rash and negligent
driving on the part of Vishal Nayal, the motorcycle bearing
Registration No. UK01-7828, dashed at Himanshu Nayal
who suffered injuries in the accident and consequently died
due to the same. The Tribunal further found that there is no
evidence on record to show that there was a collision
between the two motorcycles, or that there was any
contributory negligence on the part of the son (deceased) of
the claimants. The Tribunal further found that there is no
evidence on record, suggesting that the vehicle was being
driven without valid papers. The Tribunal also opined that
since motorcycle No. UA01-2688 was standing by the side
of the road, as such, the claim petition is not bad for non-joinder to insurance company, with whom said vehicle was

5
insured. Considering the fact that the deceased was a
student aged 18 years, his notional income ` 36,000/- per
annum was assessed and financial loss to the parents was
assessed after deducting 1/3rd of notional income, which the
deceased would have spent on himself, and the multiplier of
16 was applied.
7) Learned counsel for the appellant referred before
this Court the principle of law laid down in Sarla Verma &
others Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation. & others 2009 (2)
T.A.C. page 677 (SC) and argued that as mentioned in Para
No.15 of said judgment in the matters of death of a bachelor
person normally it should be 50% of his income which
should be deducted towards his living expenses.
8) I have considered the submission made on
behalf of the appellant and gone through the Sarla Verma's
case (Supra). Undoubtedly, the dependency of the claimants
on their son (deceased) who was a student cannot be
assessed beyond 50% of what he would have earned for the
simple reason that once he started earning, he would have
got married and also looked after his wife and children.
9) In the above circumstances, calculating 2/3rd
dependency of parents on the income of the deceased for a
period of 16 years appears to be erroneous in law. That
being so, the dependency calculated by the Tribunal should
have been at 50% as mentioned in Sarla Verma's case
(Supra).

6
10) For the reasons as discussed above, 50% of the
notional income of ` 36,000/- per annum which comes out
to be ` 18,000/- per annum should have been multiplied by
1⁄2 X 16, and the financial loss suffered by the claimants can
be said to be ` 2,88,000/-only. Adding to it funeral
expenses and consortium as granted by the Tribunal, the
actual compensation for which the claim petition should
have been allowed is ` 3,04,000/- with 6% interest per
annum thereon. There is no force on the other grounds
raised in the appeal.
11) For the reasons as discussed above, this appeal is
partly allowed, and the amount of compensation awarded by
the Tribunal is reduced from `4,00,000/- to `3,04,000/-
with 6% interest per annum thereon, which shall be paid by
the appellant to the claimants as compensation. The amount
already deposited by the appellant before the Tribunal may
be withdrawn by the claimants not exceeding ` 3,04,000/-
with 6% interest per annum thereon. The statutory deposit
before this Court may be remitted to the Tribunal
concerned.
